title: Quantity correction with no disambiguating name and genuine ambiguity safely falls through, never guesses
notes: Companion negative case to conv_326: cart has Coca-Cola at quantity 1, but the correction message claims the OLD quantity is 2 ('make the coke 3 instead of 2') -- that claim does not match reality, so both _detect_quantity_correction (old_qty=2 matches no real cart line) and _detect_named_quantity_set (two numbers present, not the single-number shape it requires) correctly decline rather than guess. Because the message DOES name a real item ('coke'), this falls through to the pre-existing, already-proven BO-000001 guard (commit f4098f6) rather than the newer quantity-correction code -- proving the new detectors never override that guard's own safety net, they only add a deterministic shortcut for the cases they are actually confident about.

turns.message: I'll have a coke (330ml) and chips
